tools.iban-validator.guide.whatIs.title: What is an IBAN?
tools.iban-validator.guide.whatIs.body.0: An IBAN (International Bank Account Number, ISO 13616) is a standardized way of writing a bank account for cross-border payments. It starts with a two-letter country code and two check digits, followed by the national account number — up to 34 characters in total.
tools.iban-validator.guide.whatIs.body.1: The check digits are computed with the mod-97 algorithm, which catches most typing errors before the money leaves your account. Around 90 countries use IBANs today — most of Europe plus parts of the Middle East, Africa and the Caribbean. The US, Canada and Australia do not.
tools.iban-validator.guide.howTo.title: How to validate an IBAN
tools.iban-validator.guide.howTo.items.0: Type or paste the IBAN into the field above — spaces and hyphens are fine.
tools.iban-validator.guide.howTo.items.1: The tool checks that the country issues IBANs and that the length matches that country's specification.
tools.iban-validator.guide.howTo.items.2: It runs the mod-97 checksum to detect typos in the digits.
tools.iban-validator.guide.howTo.items.3: The account section is compared against the country's national format, and some countries get an extra national checksum test.
tools.iban-validator.guide.howTo.items.4: If it is valid, you will see the friendly grouped format, the country and whether it is a SEPA account.
tools.iban-validator.guide.tips.title: Tips
tools.iban-validator.guide.tips.items.0: The check digits catch typos, but they do not prove the account actually exists — only the paying bank can confirm that.
tools.iban-validator.guide.tips.items.1: An IBAN identifies an account, while a SWIFT/BIC code identifies a bank — international transfers usually need both.
tools.iban-validator.guide.tips.items.2: IBANs are officially printed in groups of four characters; the tool shows this friendly format automatically.
tools.iban-validator.faqs.0.question: Which countries use IBAN?
tools.iban-validator.faqs.0.answer: About 90 countries, mainly in Europe — all EU and EEA states, the UK, Switzerland — plus the Middle East, parts of Africa, the Caribbean and a few others. The US, Canada and Australia do not use IBAN; transfers there rely on routing numbers or BSB/branch codes.
tools.iban-validator.faqs.1.question: What do the check digits do?
tools.iban-validator.faqs.1.answer: Positions 3-4 of an IBAN are two digits computed from the rest of the number with the mod-97 algorithm. If a character is mistyped or digits are swapped, the recomputed checksum almost never matches, so the error is caught before the transfer is sent.
tools.iban-validator.faqs.2.question: Is it safe to share my IBAN?
tools.iban-validator.faqs.2.answer: Yes. Your IBAN is what people need in order to pay you — it is designed to be shared, like a postal address for money. Only give it to people who are sending you money, and remember that it does not by itself authorize any debit in most countries.
tools.iban-validator.faqs.3.question: What is the difference between an IBAN and a SWIFT code?
tools.iban-validator.faqs.3.answer: They answer different questions. The IBAN identifies the individual account the money should arrive in, while the SWIFT/BIC code identifies the bank that will receive it. An international transfer form typically asks for both.

tools.screen-color-test.guide.whatIs.tit: What is the Screen Color Test?
tools.screen-color-test.guide.whatIs.bod: Screen Color Test fills your entire display with pure, uniform colors so you can inspect the panel for hardware defects: dead pixels, stuck sub-pixels and backlight bleed. It works on any monitor, laptop, tablet or phone — nothing is installed and nothing is recorded.

Each color plays a different role. Pure black in a dark room exposes backlight leaking along the edges. Pure white makes dark, never-lit pixels stand out. The red, green and blue primaries light up one sub-pixel group at a time, which is how you spot pixels that are stuck in a single color. The grayscale gradient reveals banding and uneven brightness across the panel.
tools.screen-color-test.guide.howTo.item: Set brightness to 100% and turn off night mode, dark overlay or any color filter.
Click a test color above — the whole screen fills edge to edge.
Sweep your eyes slowly across the panel, especially the edges and corners: any dot that differs from the background is a dead or stuck pixel.
Switch to pure black in a dark room and check the borders for bright, cloudy patches — that is backlight bleed.
Click, press Space or use the arrow keys to cycle colors; press Esc to exit.
tools.screen-color-test.guide.tips.title: Tips
tools.screen-color-test.guide.tips.items: Run the test in a dark room — ambient light hides faint backlight bleed.
Check every color before concluding: a stuck pixel only shows on some colors, and it can even look like a defect in an image that is actually fine.
One or two stuck pixels are covered by many manufacturers' dead-pixel policies — count them and check your warranty terms before requesting a replacement.
tools.screen-color-test.faqs.0.question: What is a dead pixel and how do I find one?
tools.screen-color-test.faqs.0.answer: A dead pixel is a pixel that stays black because its transistor no longer powers it. Fill the screen with white (and the other colors) and look for a dot that never lights up. A stuck pixel behaves the opposite way — it stays lit in one color, which the red, green and blue tests expose.
tools.screen-color-test.faqs.1.question: How do I check for backlight bleed?
tools.screen-color-test.faqs.1.answer: Set brightness to 100%, turn off the lights, and fill the screen with pure black. Look at the edges and corners: bright, cloudy patches mean the backlight is leaking through the panel. A small amount is normal on most LCD laptops; it only matters if it is visible in everyday use.
tools.screen-color-test.faqs.2.question: Can a dead pixel be fixed?
tools.screen-color-test.faqs.2.answer: Usually not. Dead pixels are a hardware defect, and many manufacturers replace the panel under their dead-pixel policy if there are enough of them. Rapidly flashing colors sometimes revives stuck pixels, but results are not guaranteed.
tools.screen-color-test.faqs.3.question: Does the test work on phones and tablets?
tools.screen-color-test.faqs.3.answer: Yes. Tap a color to start, tap the screen to cycle colors. On iPhones the browser cannot hide its address bar, so rotate to fullscreen video or use the Add to Home Screen PWA for a distraction-free check.

tools.screen-color-picker.faqs.1.questio: Why is the button disabled for me?
tools.screen-color-picker.faqs.1.answer: The eyedropper requires the browser's EyeDropper API, supported by Chrome, Edge, Opera, and Safari 17.2+. Firefox and some older browsers don't support it yet — switch to Chrome, Edge, or a recent Safari to use this tool.
tools.screen-color-picker.faqs.2.questio: Is the color data sent anywhere?
tools.screen-color-picker.faqs.2.answer: No. Everything runs locally in your browser. Your picked colors are only stored in your browser's localStorage so your recent picks persist between visits — they are never transmitted.
tools.screen-color-picker.faqs.3.questio: What's the difference from Image Color Picker?
tools.screen-color-picker.faqs.3.answer: Image Color Picker samples colors inside an uploaded picture. This screen picker grabs colors from your actual display without any upload — use it when you want to match a color you see anywhere on your screen.
tools.screen-color-picker.faqs.4.questio: How do I copy a color?
tools.screen-color-picker.faqs.4.answer: After picking, the current color shows Hex, RGB, and HSL values, each with a one-click copy button. Your recent picks appear below as swatches you can click to recall.

tools.screen-color-picker.guide.steps.2: Copy the Hex, RGB, or HSL value with one click.

tools.multiavatar-avatar-generator.title: Multiavatar Avatar Generator
tools.multiavatar-avatar-generator.descr: Generate a unique multicultural avatar from any text. Every string produces its own distinct avatar — perfect for profile pictures, gaming logos, and identicons. Runs entirely in your browser.
Does the same text always produce the same avatar?
Yes. Multiavatar works like an identicon — the text is hashed into a set of numbers that pick the avatar's parts. Type the same text again and you get the exact same avatar every time.
Are my avatars uploaded to a server?
No. The generator runs entirely in your browser using a small client-side library. Nothing you type is ever sent anywhere, and no data is stored.
Can I use the generated avatars commercially?
Yes, the Multiavatar library is free for commercial use. Generated avatars may be used on websites, apps, products, and social profiles without restriction.
SVG for a scalable vector image (crisp at any size) and PNG at 512x512 for easy use on websites, apps, and social profiles. Toggle "Remove background circle" for a head-only avatar.
The algorithm combines 48 base designs into 48^6 = 12,230,590,464 possible avatars. Some parts are intentionally similar, but every text string maps to its own distinct avatar.

tools.video-compressor.faqs.0.question: How much can I compress a video?
tools.video-compressor.faqs.0.answer: Typically 50-90% reduction depending on the original quality and your compression settings. A 100 MB video can often be reduced to 10-30 MB at medium quality with little visible difference.
tools.video-compressor.faqs.1.question: Does compressing a video reduce quality?
tools.video-compressor.faqs.1.answer: Some quality loss is inherent in compression, but at medium-high settings the difference is barely noticeable. The tool lets you preview the result before downloading so you can find the right balance.
tools.video-compressor.faqs.2.question: What video formats are supported?
tools.video-compressor.faqs.2.answer: Upload MP4, WebM, or MOV files. The compressed output is always MP4 (H.264) which is universally compatible with all devices and platforms.
tools.video-compressor.faqs.3.question: Is my video uploaded to a server?
tools.video-compressor.faqs.3.answer: No. All compression happens locally in your browser using FFmpeg WebAssembly. Your video never leaves your device. Nothing is stored anywhere.
tools.video-compressor.faqs.4.question: Why is compression slow?
tools.video-compressor.faqs.4.answer: Video encoding is CPU-intensive work. Processing happens in your browser via WebAssembly, which is slower than native software. Shorter videos and lower resolutions process faster.
tools.video-compressor.faqs.5.question: Can I compress videos for email or Discord?
tools.video-compressor.faqs.5.answer: Yes. Email typically limits attachments to 25 MB, Discord free tier to 25 MB. Use medium or high compression to get your video under these limits.

tools.resume-builder.faqs.1.question: How do I download my resume as a PDF?
tools.resume-builder.faqs.1.answer: Click 'Download PDF' and your browser's print dialog will open. Select 'Save as PDF' as the destination. This preserves the exact layout and formatting of your resume.
tools.resume-builder.faqs.2.question: Is my data safe?
tools.resume-builder.faqs.2.answer: Your resume data never leaves your device. Everything is processed locally in your browser — nothing is uploaded to any server. Close the tab and all data is gone.
tools.resume-builder.faqs.3.question: What resume format should I use?
tools.resume-builder.faqs.3.answer: For most job applications, a reverse-chronological format works best — list your most recent experience first. The Classic and Modern templates both use this format. Use Minimal for creative roles or when you want a clean, simple look.
tools.resume-builder.faqs.4.question: Can I use this resume for ATS (Applicant Tracking Systems)?
tools.resume-builder.faqs.4.answer: Yes. All templates output clean, readable text that ATS systems can parse. Avoid using images or complex graphics in your resume content for best ATS compatibility.
tools.resume-builder.faqs.5.question: How long should my resume be?
tools.resume-builder.faqs.5.answer: One page for early-career professionals (0-10 years). Two pages are acceptable for senior roles with extensive experience. Keep it concise — recruiters spend an average of 6-7 seconds on initial resume screening.

tools.video-watermark-remover.title: Video Watermark Remover
tools.video-watermark-remover.descriptio: Remove watermarks from any video for free. Smart Remove and Blur modes. No upload, no signup, runs entirely in your browser.
tools.video-watermark-remover.faqs.0.que: How do I remove a watermark from a video for free?
tools.video-watermark-remover.faqs.0.ans: Upload your video to this tool, draw a rectangle over the watermark, choose Smart Remove or Blur mode, and click Remove Watermark. Everything runs in your browser — no upload, no signup.
tools.video-watermark-remover.faqs.1.que: What is the difference between Smart Remove and Blur?
tools.video-watermark-remover.faqs.1.ans: Smart Remove uses FFmpeg's delogo filter to intelligently interpolate surrounding pixels into the watermark area, producing natural-looking results. Blur applies a heavy Gaussian blur that completely obscures the watermark — useful when Smart Remove leaves artifacts on complex backgrounds.
tools.video-watermark-remover.faqs.2.que: Does removing a video watermark reduce quality?
tools.video-watermark-remover.faqs.2.ans: The tool uses FFmpeg with high-quality encoding (CRF 20) so the rest of your video stays sharp. Only the selected watermark region is modified. Audio is copied without re-encoding.
tools.video-watermark-remover.faqs.3.que: Is there a file size or video length limit?
tools.video-watermark-remover.faqs.3.ans: There is no hard limit since all processing happens locally in your browser. Smart Remove and Blur both handle long videos efficiently.
tools.video-watermark-remover.faqs.4.que: Can I remove watermarks from TikTok or YouTube videos?
tools.video-watermark-remover.faqs.4.ans: Yes, as long as you have the video file downloaded. Upload the MP4, WebM, or MOV file and select the watermark area.
tools.video-watermark-remover.faqs.5.que: Is my video uploaded to a server?
tools.video-watermark-remover.faqs.5.ans: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser using WebAssembly-powered FFmpeg. Your video never leaves your device.
tools.video-watermark-remover.guide.what: What Is the Video Watermark Remover?

The Video Watermark Remover is a free browser-based tool that removes watermarks, logos, and text overlays from any video file. It uses FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly, running entirely in your browser with no server uploads.
tools.video-watermark-remover.guide.mode: Smart Remove — Uses FFmpeg's delogo filter to interpolate surrounding pixels into the watermark area. Fast and effective for most watermarks, especially on simple or uniform backgrounds.
Blur — Applies a heavy Gaussian blur that completely obscures the watermark. Use when Smart Remove leaves artifacts, or when the watermark is on a very complex moving background.
tools.video-watermark-remover.guide.howT: Upload your video file (MP4, WebM, MOV).
Scrub the timeline to find a frame where the watermark is visible.
Click and drag a rectangle tightly around the watermark.
Click Remove Watermark and wait for processing.
tools.video-watermark-remover.guide.tips: Draw the rectangle as tightly as possible — a smaller selection produces cleaner results.
Smart Remove works best for semi-transparent stock watermarks and text on uniform backgrounds.
Use Blur as a fallback when Smart Remove leaves visible artifacts.

tools.photo-watermark-remover.descriptio: Remove watermarks from photos completely free. No signup, no limits. Your image never leaves your browser — all processing happens locally.
tools.photo-watermark-remover.faqs.0.que: How do I remove a watermark from a photo for free?
tools.photo-watermark-remover.faqs.0.ans: Upload your image, paint over the watermark with the brush tool (it appears as a red overlay), and click Remove Watermark. The tool uses an inpainting algorithm to fill the area with surrounding pixel data. Everything runs locally in your browser.
tools.photo-watermark-remover.faqs.1.que: Does removing a photo watermark affect image quality?
tools.photo-watermark-remover.faqs.1.ans: The inpainting algorithm only modifies the pixels you paint over. The rest of the image remains completely untouched. You can download the result at full original resolution as a PNG file.
